query: Casting is the predominant fabrication method for high-entropy alloys, but solidification-related porosity and microstructural nonuniformity can cause heterogeneous properties. Studies of other high-entropy-alloy compositions have reported high hardness and notable compressive performance, yet these findings do not establish how to improve CoCrFeNiTi; moreover, some investigated alloys were brittle at 25 °C and displayed only limited plastic deformation at 600 °C. For equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi with a simple crystal structure, favorable plasticity and machinability, but low hardness and load-bearing capability, what single intervention could improve hardness and mechanical performance while preserving those favorable characteristics and clarifying the relationship between microstructure and deformation? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, a quantitative prediction relative to the unmodified alloy, the processing and testing boundaries within which it should apply, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled microstructural and mechanical experiment with explicit falsification criteria.

generation.hypothesis: The introduction of a controlled amount of carbon (C) as an alloying element into the equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi high-entropy alloy through powder metallurgy will improve its hardness and mechanical performance while preserving favorable plasticity and machinability.
generation.material_initial_state: Equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi high-entropy alloy with a simple crystal structure
generation.intervention: Addition of a controlled amount of carbon (C) as an alloying element
generation.conditions: Powder metallurgy processing, subsequent heat treatment if necessary
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of carbide precipitates or solid solution strengthening
generation.mechanism: The added carbon will form carbide precipitates or dissolve into the lattice, creating solid solution strengthening effects that enhance the alloy's hardness and mechanical performance without significantly compromising its plasticity and machinability
generation.predicted_outcome: An increase in hardness by at least 15% and an improvement in compressive yield strength by at least 10% compared to the unmodified alloy, while maintaining a ductility of at least 5% elongation at room temperature
generation.baseline: Unmodified equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi alloy
generation.boundary: Processing temperatures below 1200°C, testing temperatures between -20°C and 600°C, and strain rates applicable to standard mechanical testing
generation.uncertainty: The optimal amount of carbon to add, the exact nature of the carbide precipitates or solid solution effects, and how these will interact with the complex microstructure of the high-entropy alloy to influence mechanical properties

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of specimens: one from the unmodified CoCrFeNiTi alloy and another from the carbon-modified alloy. Conduct microstructural analysis (SEM, TEM) and mechanical testing (hardness, compression, tensile testing) under the specified conditions.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the carbon-modified alloy does not exhibit at least a 15% increase in hardness and a 10% increase in compressive yield strength compared to the unmodified alloy, or if its ductility falls below 5% elongation at room temperature, the hypothesis is falsified.
